title: omicstra: a multi-agent MCP server for cross-modal embedding alignment and evidence-based routing in spatial biology
description:
A multi-agent MCP server for cross-modal embedding alignment, fusion, and evidence-based routing in spatial biology. Modality-specialized agents and their integration are orchestrated with LangGraph; foundation-model encoders are pluggable; integration strategy is a configurable experimental dimension. Alignments are evaluated against declared metrics, and questions are routed from a cohort's own recorded evidence, refusing when that evidence is absent rather than inheriting another cohort's result. Agents are deterministic components with persistent context; the server ships no model.

v1.1 completes the compute path and the evidence path. v1.0 shipped the read path - inventory, EDA, admissibility gate and routing - over stdio and HTTP, with the seed cohort's evidence pack committed so a fresh clone can route without training anything. This release adds: encode, niche join and evaluation as compute stages, each refused into any declared read-only path; the Virchow2 encoder port verified against the cached embeddings that produced the published grid; six guards as gates over pinned artifacts for H1 through H3; omicstra promote, which computes the evidence pack's candidates, intervals, floors, guard verdicts and outcome from artifacts and takes only its prose from a person; a cohort-free report renderer; and omicstra run, the end-to-end command that defines v1.1, with a diff that rebuilds the published pack from the artifacts - on the seed cohort every value and interval reproduces.

creators.name: Sanati, Nasim
creators.affiliation: Sears Lab, Brenden-Colson Center, OHSU Knight Cancer Institute

notes: Funded by the ResearchHub Foundation (doi:10.55277/researchhub.6ou1w3h3). Seed cohort: 92 triple-negative breast cancer patients from Wang et al. 2024, Nature Communications 15:10232 - original Spatial Transcriptomics platform, co-registered with H&E whole-slide images. The package ships no cohort data; it is pointed at a cohort directory.
